paper_metadata.title: Review of Automatic and Semi-Automatic Creation of Knowledge Graphs from Structured and Unstructured Data
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of RTA-CSIT 2023; CEUR Workshop Proceedings
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper reviews recent work on automatic and semi-automatic knowledge-graph creation from structured and unstructured data. It considers handling unstructured text, defining nodes and relationships, ontology development, commonly used machine-learning/NLP algorithms, Neo4j, and Python; it concludes that semi-automatic approaches exist while fully automatic approaches remain ideas.

problem_addressed: A systematic review of whether and how knowledge graphs can be created automatically or semi-automatically from structured/tabular or unstructured data, motivated by expert-built domain KGs being time-consuming, error-prone, and unsuitable for large-scale or fast-changing domains.

methodology.primary_family: Systematic literature review (not a Text-to-KG methodology family in the supplied taxonomy)
methodology.description: The authors searched IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer Link, and ACM Digital Library for 2017–December 2022 using one Boolean query. They deduplicated records; removed books, chapters, surveys, and reviews; screened keywords and abstracts with a second reviewer resolving doubts; then read full papers and reached reviewer consensus. The resulting 19 accessible studies are narratively analyzed by domain, degree of automation, extraction/linking/preprocessing, ontology use, algorithms, storage, and tools.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Ontology and schema construction are review topics. The reviewed methods use task-specific ontologies, ontology suites combining taxonomy enrichment and relation discovery, automated class suggestions, Protégé-built ontologies, and the DISK ontology; the review reports that some reviewed papers did not specify an ontology.

input_output.input_type: Review corpus of papers about structured/tabular/relational-database data and unstructured natural-language text used for knowledge-graph creation.
input_output.input_granularity: Paper-level review corpus; the reviewed systems variously process text facts/spans, free text, electronic medical records, table cells, datasets, and relational/tabular data.
input_output.output_representation: Review synthesis of automatic/semi-automatic KG-creation approaches; reviewed output forms include subject–predicate–object facts/triples, entity-property-relationship graphs, Neo4j nodes and edges/property graphs, and RDF triples.

datasets: Literature-review corpus: 1,027 initial candidate papers retrieved from IEEE Xplore, Springer Link, ScienceDirect, and ACM Digital Library; 19 accessible papers analyzed in depth.
Reviewed-study domains reported: medicine, education, research papers, welding, retail, biodiversity, geographic data, course/MOOC data, and electronic medical records.

metrics: Review-retrieval and screening counts: 1,027 total search results; IEEE Xplore 232; Springer Link 288; ScienceDirect 342; ACM Digital Library 165.
Screening counts: 56 papers after the first keyword/abstract review; 21 selected for in-depth review; 19 papers analyzed because two full texts were unavailable.
No model-level predictive metrics, statistical tests, or common benchmark metrics are reported for this review paper.
evaluation.setting: PRISMA-guided systematic-review process. Search period: 2017 through December 2022. Sources: IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer Link, and ACM Digital Library. Selection was limited to journal and conference papers; duplicate records, books/chapters, surveys, and reviews were removed; title/keyword/abstract screening and then full-paper review were performed, with reviewer consensus for doubtful cases.

value: The search yielded 1,027 potential papers; 56 remained after initial screening, 21 were selected for in-depth review, and 19 were analyzed because two papers could not be obtained as complete documents.
The review identifies medicine and education as the most represented reviewed domains, followed by research-paper graphs and diverse other domains.
The review finds both semi-automatic and claimed automatic approaches, but concludes that fully automatic KG creation remains an idea rather than an established outcome.

Across the reviewed work, information extraction, entity linking, entity/relation identification, data cleaning, synonym handling, ontology construction/use, machine-learning/NLP methods, and graph storage are recurring components.

The authors conclude that important data and relationships can be extracted from created KGs with machine-learning methods and state that well-structured data/relationships, well-designed ontologies, and advanced algorithms support useful construction.

value: Author-stated: The review covers both structured and unstructured data and considers multiple KG-construction components, including text handling, nodes/relations, and ontology development.
Author-stated: It uses a stated PRISMA-based procedure, names four search libraries, provides its exact search string and date range, and reports the screening flow.

Review-level inference: The paper is useful as a compact map of heterogeneous KG-creation components, algorithms, tools, and application domains, including semi-automatic workflows that combine manual and automatic work.

value: Author-stated: The search may have missed relevant papers from other databases, excluded non-English papers, and lacked full-text access to two selected papers.
Author-stated: The fast-growing and multidisciplinary KG literature makes the review difficult.

Review-level inference: The single narrow Boolean query is centered on databases/relational databases and may under-retrieve Text-to-KG work described with NLP, information extraction, triples, entities, relation extraction, or ontology terms but not the exact query terms.

Review-level inference: The paper does not provide a per-study extraction table, study-quality assessment, reproducible record-level bibliography/screening log, or quantitative cross-study comparison; therefore its claims are primarily narrative and should not be used as comparative performance evidence.

Review-level inference: Evaluate automatic and semi-automatic KG-construction methods separately using compatible end-to-end measures for extraction accuracy, ontology/schema quality, graph quality, human effort, coverage, and reproducibility.
